'''''Cucurbita moschata''''' is a species originating in the tropical Americas<ref name="Hui">{{cite book |title=Handbook of Food Science, Technology, and Engineering |volume=1 |pages=20–10 |chapter=Pumpkins and Squashes |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=43sA1NhzCWsC&pg=SA20-PA10 |first=Yiu H. |last=Hui |publisher=CRC Press |location=Boca Raton, Florida |year=2006 |isbn=9781420027518 }}</ref> which is cultivated for edible flesh, flowers, greens, and seeds.<ref name="Boswell"/> It includes [[cultivar]]s known in English as [[Squash (plant)|squash]] or [[pumpkin]]. Cultivars of ''C. moschata'' are generally more tolerant of hot, humid weather than squash of other domesticated species. ''C. moschata'' also exhibit a greater resistance to certain disease and insects, notably including to the [[squash vine borer]]. Commercially-made [[pumpkin pie]] mix is most often made from varieties of ''C. moschata''.

==History==
All species of squashes and pumpkins are native to the Western Hemisphere, and the ancestral members of the genus ''[[Cucurbita]]'' were present in the Americas before humans.<ref name="Boswell">{{cite magazine |author=Victor E. Boswell |name-list-style=and |author2=Else Bostelmann|title=Our Vegetable Travelers |magazine=The National Geographic Magazine|volume=96|issue=2|date= August 1949}}</ref> Squash are important food plants of the original people of the region, ranking next to maize and beans in many precolonial American economies.<ref name="Boswell"/>

In the modern era, ''C. moschata'' has been one of the most widely cultivated Cucurbita in the tropics. Even so, it has been proposed that production statistics do not reflect its true proliferation because it is often grown on a small-scale basis for local consumption. The greatest diversity among ''C. moschata'' populations can be found in the tropical Americas, suggesting a center of origin in that region. Various areas have been proposed for the origin, with one recent candidate area in northwestern South America.<ref name="cucurbit-2004">{{Cite journal |last1=Thomas |first1=Andres |last2=Lebeda |first2=Aleš |last3=Paris |first3=Harry |date=2004 |title=Diversity in tropical pumpkin (Cucurbita moschata): cultivar origin and history |url=https://cucurbit.info/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/cuc2004proceedings.pdf#page=113 |journal=Cucurbit Network}}</ref>

==Systematics==
No modern Cucurbita species is considered fully genetically isolated and ''C. moschata'' can be hybridized with any other species in the genus. It has been suggested that this shows that the species of ''Cucurbita'' have diversified more recently than those of related genera such as ''[[Cucumis]]'' and ''[[Citrullus]]''.<ref name="whitaker">{{cite journal |last1=Whitaker |first1=Thomas W. |last2=Bemis |first2=W. P. |year=1975 |title=Origin and Evolution of the Cultivated ''Cucurbita'' |journal=[[Torrey Botanical Society|Bulletin of the Torrey Botanical Club]] |volume=102 |issue=6 |pages=362–368 |publisher=Torrey Botanical Society |location=New York |jstor=2484762 |doi=10.2307/2484762 }}</ref>

Historically, varieties of cushaw squash now classified as ''[[Cucurbita argyrosperma]]'' were assigned to ''Cucurbita moschata''. A small number of ''C. moschata'' varieties are still commonly known as cushaws. Genetic research indicates that, while distinct species, ''C. argyrosperma'' and ''C. moschata'' are closely related.<ref name="biology-utilization">{{Cite book |last=Merrick |first=Laura |url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/10.7591/j.ctvr7f7q4.11 |chapter=Systematics and Evolution of a Domesticated Squash, Curcubita argyrosperma, and Its Wild and Weedy Relatives |title=Biology and Utilization of the Cucurbitaceae |date=2019-05-15 |pages=77–95 |publisher=Cornell University Press |jstor=10.7591/j.ctvr7f7q4.11 |isbn=978-1-5017-4544-7 |language=en}}</ref>

===Cultivars===
''Variety'' is used here interchangeably with ''cultivar'', but not with ''species'' or taxonomic variety.
* [[Al Hachi]] – a [[winter squash]] used in [[Kashmir]], usually dried
* [[Aehobak]] – a [[summer squash]], also called ''Korean zucchini''
* Brazilian crook neck, Abóbora de pescoço or Abóbora seca – a large, curved-neck variety with deep orange flesh and dark green skin with light orange highlights found in Brazil.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gosto |first1=Brasil a. |title=Abóbora-de-Pescoço |url=https://brasilagosto.org/abobora-de-pescoco/ |publisher=Instituto Brasil a Gosto |access-date=25 November 2021 |date=28 June 2019 }}</ref>
* [[Butternut squash]] – a popular [[winter squash]] in much of North America, Europe and South Africa.
* [[Calabaza]] – a commonly grown winter squash in the [[Caribbean]], tropical America, and the Philippines
* [[Dickinson pumpkin]] – [[Libby's]] uses a proprietary strain of Dickinson for its canned pumpkin<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pumpkins |url=https://www.agmrc.org/commodities-products/vegetables/pumpkins |access-date=26 May 2023 |website=www.agmrc.org |language=en-us }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Arumugam |first=Nadia |title=Why You Want Canned Pumpkin For A Better Pie, Not Fresh |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/nadiaarumugam/2013/11/19/why-you-want-canned-pumpkin-for-a-better-pie-not-fresh/ |access-date=26 May 2023 |website=Forbes |language=en }}</ref>
* Giromon – a large, green cultivar, grown primarily in the [[Caribbean]]. Haitians use it to make the traditional "soupe giromon".<ref name="AC">{{cite book |last=West-Duran |first=Alan |title=African Caribbeans: a reference guide |year=2003 |page=110 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EH8ESDc9FAUC&q=giromon+soup&pg=PA110 |publisher=Greenwood Press |location=Westport, CT |isbn=0-313-31240-0 }}</ref>
* Golden Cushaw – Similar in shape but a different species than the common ''[[Cucurbita argyrosperma]]'' "cushaw" type.<ref name="NGA">{{Cite web |title=NGA Plant database entry for Cushaw Pumpkin (Cucurbita moschata 'Golden Cushaw') with one image and 7 data details |url=https://garden.org/plants/view/116811/Cushaw-Pumpkin-Cucurbita-moschata-Golden-Cushaw/ |access-date=2025-01-25 |website=garden.org |language=en}}</ref><ref name="daves">{{Cite web |title=PlantFiles: The Largest Plant Identification Reference Guide - Dave's Garden - Golden Cushaw |url=https://davesgarden.com/guides/pf/go/61083 |access-date=2025-01-25 |website=davesgarden.com}}</ref>
* Loche – a [[landrace]] of squashes from Peru.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Andres TC|author2= R Ugás|author3= F Bustamante|year= 2006|title= Loche: A unique pre-Columbian squash locally grown in North Coastal Peru |journal=Proceedings of Cucurbitaceae 2006|editor=G.J. Holmes |publisher= Universal Press|location= Raleigh, North Carolina, USA |pages= 333–340|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/237805567}}</ref>
* Liscia – grows early in the season, reaching maturation after 115 to 130 days<ref name="Maťová">{{cite journal |last1=Maťová |first1=Adriána |last2=Hegedűsová |first2=Alžbeta |last3=Andrejiová |first3=Alena |last4=Hegedűs |first4=Ondrej |last5=Golian |first5=Marcel |last6=Šlosár |first6=Miroslav |last7=Lidiková |first7=Judita |last8=Lošák |first8=Tomáš |title=Evaluation of Storage and Freezing, Baking, and Boiling Treatments on Total Carotenoids Content in the Fruits of Selected Cucurbita moschata Duch. Varieties |journal=Journal of Food Quality |date=11 May 2021 |volume=2021 |pages=1–9 |doi=10.1155/2021/5584652 |url=https://downloads.hindawi.com/journals/jfq/2021/5584652.pdf |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* Long Island cheese pumpkin – the exterior resembles a wheel of cheese in shape, color, and texture
* Musquée de Provence, Moscata di Provenza or Fairytale pumpkin – a large hybrid from France with sweet, fragrant, deep-orange flesh often sold by the slice due to its size.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://whatscookingamerica.net/squash.htm |title=Squash |website=What's Cooking America |date=13 November 2015 |access-date=25 November 2021 }}</ref>
* Naples long squash or Courge pleine de Naples – a large, long squash with deep green skin and small bulb at the end. It is 10 to 25 kg on average and found in France and Italy<ref name="Courge Pleine de Naples">{{cite web |last1=Marie |first1=Isa |title=La Courge Pleine de Naples |url=https://www.grelinettecassolettes.com/article-la-courge-pleine-de-naples-84264611.html |website=Grelinette et Cassolettes |date=14 September 2011 |access-date=25 November 2021 }}</ref>
* São Paulo pumpkin or Abóbora paulista is a butternut-shaped variety with well-defined white and green stripes along its length
* [[Seminole pumpkin]] – an heirloom variety originally cultivated by the [[Seminole]] people of what is now Florida<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Castetter |first=Edward F. |date=1930 |title=Species Crosses in the Genus Cucurbita |url=https://scholarworks.uni.edu/context/pias/article/5923/viewcontent/021_Species_Crosses_in_the_Genus_Cucurbita.pdf |journal=American Journal of Botany |volume=17 |issue=1 |pages=41–57 |doi=10.2307/2446379 |jstor=2446379 |issn=0002-9122 }}</ref>
* [[Tromboncino (squash)|Tromboncino]] – a summer squash, also known as "Zucchetta"<ref name="WSU">{{cite web |title=Zucchetta |url=http://agsyst.wsu.edu/zucchetta.html |work=Mount Vernon Northwestern Washington Research and Extension Center: Vegetable Research and Extension |publisher=Washington State University |access-date=10 May 2013 }}</ref>
